story.title: Why Hawaii's Rat Fix Became a Bird Problem
story.opening_object: rat, cane field, mongoose and nest

steps.label: Birds guarded from the rat fix
steps.situation: Ground-nesting birds are now protected from the animal brought in to control rats.

steps.label: Rats in the cane
steps.situation: Rats damage sugar cane in Hawaii and a living control agent looks promising.

steps.label: Mongooses introduced
steps.situation: Mongooses are deliberately introduced to the islands to control the rat population.

steps.label: The explanation that stops at the clock
steps.situation: The familiar account -- mongooses by day, rats by night -- is the tidy version that gets repeated.

steps.label: What else the mongoose eats
steps.situation: The mongoose takes ground-nesting birds and eggs, an interaction the plan never counted.

steps.label: Harm that geography makes lasting
steps.situation: A mongoose lives across several habitats, so the harm spreads and persists.

steps.label: Kauai's first capture
steps.situation: In May 2012 the first live mongoose on Kauai is trapped near Lihue; the islands are now managing the fix.
